title: Overview — the widget contract
description: Why widgets are self-contained, what the file layout looks like, and a short tour of the five mandatory wiring points before we walk through them in depth.

data.markdown:
## Self-contained widgets, one wiring contract

In `src/widgets/`, every widget is **self-contained**: it owns its data schema, its read-mode component, its editor form, and a single registry entry. No other module needs to know it exists — except for one carefully placed list of variants in `src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts` that lets the widget round-trip through saved lesson JSON.

That isolation is only possible because every new widget honors a fixed wiring contract. Skip a step and you get one of three failure modes:

- The widget renders but its **chrome has no accent colour** (forgot the CSS var).
- The build script **errors during `npm run build:schemas`** (forgot to register the data schema).
- The widget renders fine in memory but **lesson JSON containing it is rejected by the API on save / load** (forgot the `SectionSchema` variant).

:::callout{type="info" title="Read this alongside the README"}
This course mirrors the contract documented in `src/widgets/README.md` — the README is the source of truth, this course is the readable, executable companion. Whenever a path or function name in the lessons looks unfamiliar, open the README and the cited file side by side.
:::

The Histogram widget at `src/widgets/Histogram/` follows every step of the contract and is the recommended copy-paste starting point. We will use it as the canonical worked example throughout the course.

sections.title: File layout for a new widget

data.markdown:
## What ships in `src/widgets/<Name>/`

Every widget lives under `src/widgets/<Name>/` with at least four files:

```
src/widgets/
  registry.ts             — central type→component registry (you EXTEND this)
  Widget.tsx              — shared chrome (header, status badge, accent rail)
  schemas/
    build.ts              — npm run build:schemas writes <type>.json here (you EXTEND this)
  <Name>/
    schema.ts             — Zod schema + inferred TS type
    <Name>Widget.tsx      — read/render component, props: { data: <Type>Data }
    <Name>Editor.tsx      — side-panel form, props: { initial, onCancel, onSave }
    sample.ts             — typed sample data (used by fixtures, init skills)
```

Three files **outside** the new widget folder also need a small edit:

- `src/widgets/registry.ts` — add one entry in `widgetRegistry` plus one literal in the `WidgetType` union.
- `src/widgets/schemas/build.ts` — add one import + one entry in the `widgets` map.
- `src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts` — add one new `<Name>SectionSchema` plus one entry in the `SectionSchema` discriminated union.

And one stylesheet:

- `src/styles/tokens.css` — add a `--widget-<name>` CSS variable in **both** the light and dark theme blocks.

That is the whole contract. The next lesson walks through each touch point in order, with the Histogram widget as the worked example.

## The contract at a glance

The order matters: each step depends on the one before it, and skipping any of them produces a runtime error or breaks the schema build.

1. **CSS var `--widget-<name>`** in `src/styles/tokens.css` (light + dark blocks).
2. **Zod data schema** at `src/widgets/<Name>/schema.ts`, plus a registration in `src/widgets/schemas/build.ts` so `npm run build:schemas` emits `<name>.json`.
3. **`widgetRegistry` entry** in `src/widgets/registry.ts` (`component` / `label` / `icon` / `accentVar`) and a new literal in the `WidgetType` union.
4. **Per-widget editor form** at `src/widgets/<Name>/<Name>Editor.tsx`, plus branches in `WidgetEditPanel` and `SectionRenderer` inside `src/app/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug]/page.tsx`.
5. **`SectionSchema` variant** in `src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts` — without this, lesson JSON containing the widget is rejected by `PUT /api/courses/<slug>/lessons/<lessonSlug>` even though the read-mode component renders.

:::callout{type="warning" title="Step 5 is easy to forget"}
Steps 1–4 are enough to get the widget rendering on screen during local development. The bug only surfaces on the next round-trip through the API — typically at "Save" time after editing or after a fresh server restart that re-validates lesson files. **Always add the `SectionSchema` variant** unless you have a very specific reason not to.
:::

sections.title: The canonical Histogram example, rendered live

data.markdown:
The bar chart above is rendered by `HistogramWidget` (`src/widgets/Histogram/HistogramWidget.tsx`) reading the section's `data` against `HistogramDataSchema` (`src/widgets/Histogram/schema.ts`). Two arrays — `binEdges` and `counts` — are all the JSON the widget needs. The accent colour on the rail and the slider thumb both come from the `--widget-histogram` CSS variable defined in `src/styles/tokens.css`.

In the next lesson we follow the exact path that produced this rendering, step by step, with the actual snippets from the Histogram source files.

sections.title: Quick check: which steps are mandatory?

data.question: Which of the following are mandatory wiring points when adding a new widget type? (Select all that apply.)
options: Adding a `--widget-<name>` CSS variable in src/styles/tokens.css (both light and dark blocks)
Registering the Zod schema in src/widgets/schemas/build.ts so `npm run build:schemas` emits a JSON Schema
Adding a `<Name>SectionSchema` to the discriminated union in src/lib/schemas/lesson.ts
Writing a custom Storybook story for the widget under stories/
Adding an entry to `widgetRegistry` in src/widgets/registry.ts and extending the `WidgetType` union
data.explanation: Four of the five steps are present here: the CSS var (step 1), the Zod schema + build.ts entry (step 2), the registry entry (step 3), and the SectionSchema variant (step 5). Step 4 — the per-widget editor and lesson-page wiring — is implied by the editor form requirement covered later in the course. There is no Storybook in this codebase; the `sample.ts` fixture replaces it for fixtures and init skills.
